body:
Global crypto markets gave back ground on Sunday, with total market cap sliding to $2.57T, a -5.24% decline in 24 hours on $91.8B in volume. The session had the texture of a controlled exhale rather than a panic — Fear and Greed printed 66 today against 71 yesterday, so sentiment is cooling but greed hasn't left the building. BTC dominance held at 59.2% and ETH dominance at 11.2%, which tells you the bid is rotating defensively back into large caps as altcoins bleed harder. The week was genuinely impressive across the board, and today looks like the market digesting that move rather than reversing it.

Bitcoin traded at $76,239, off -1.70% in the past 24 hours but still sitting on a +20.70% 7-day gain with $29.0B in volume behind it. That weekly print confirms what CoinDesk is calling a "squeeze-led" rally — bears got decimated, and the survivors are now cautious rather than aggressive. The hourly tick of -0.10% suggests the selling pressure is light and relatively orderly. The key question is whether $76,239 acts as a consolidation floor or a launching pad for distribution; given BTC dominance holding above 59%, the market is not yet in the rotation mode that typically precedes the next leg down. Watch the $74,000 region as the first meaningful support and $78,500 as the level bulls need to reclaim to signal continuation.

Ethereum at $2,393.53 outperformed BTC on the week with a +27.00% 7-day move, though the 24-hour print of -2.10% on $14.84B volume shows it is not immune to today's broader softness. Among altcoins, XRP is the session's most notable story: +44.00% on the week but -5.80% in 24 hours on $7.06B volume, suggesting significant profit-taking after a violent squeeze. ADA and DOT are today's underperformers at -7.60% and -8.10% respectively, and both carry thin volume — ADA at $0.71B and DOT at a notably light $0.13B — which means these are not capitulation prints but rather air pockets left by buyers stepping away. On the positive side, UNI is the relative standout, off only -0.80% in 24 hours while booking a +25.70% weekly gain, and LINK and BNB are also holding up comparatively well intraday. The Sandbox exploit that forced a halt to Base and BNB chain bridging is worth monitoring for contagion into gaming and metaverse tokens, though BNB at $687.17 has so far absorbed it at only -2.00% for the session.

The macro backdrop is doing more work than most participants are acknowledging. Ray Dalio telling investors to buy "a bit" of Bitcoin amid a potential debt crisis is the kind of institutional signal that reinforces the structural bid under this market even when the daily candle is red. The Bitget CEO's view that Bitcoin remains near current levels at year-end and his skepticism around a US strategic Bitcoin reserve purchase introduces a ceiling narrative worth tracking. On the regulatory side, MiCA pressure on DeFi vaults is building per Cointelegraph, and Kalshi is now off-limits in multiple states as prediction markets and the CFTC sharpen their positions — these are not immediate price catalysts but they are incrementally tightening the operating environment for DeFi and structured onchain products. The tokenized stocks warning from the Fairmint CEO referencing Wall Street's 1960s paper crisis adds a longer-term structural caution to what has otherwise been a bullish narrative around real-world assets.

The week ahead pivots on whether Bitcoin can hold above $74,000 and reclaim $78,500, which would flush the remaining short overhang and set up a test of the $80,000 psychological level. The primary risk is a continuation of today's altcoin softness spreading into ETH and dragging BTC dominance lower in a disorderly way, particularly if the Sandbox exploit widens or triggers further bridge suspensions across chains. Watch XRP closely — at -5.80% today after a +44.00% week, the next 48 hours will reveal whether that was healthy digestion or the start of a sharper mean-reversion. The Fear and Greed drop from 71 to 66 is not alarming, but a move below 60 would signal that the squeeze narrative has fully run its course and the market is repricing risk. BitMart's potential partial restart and creditor payouts could add headline noise to exchange risk sentiment but is unlikely to move the broader tape materially. Stay long quality, watch leverage, and treat any move below $74,000 on BTC as a trigger for reassessment.
